title: Sable and the Safehouse
premise: Coral Brightwater, a financial-crimes investigator who has spent a decade untangling laundered fortunes, is approached by Sable, a stranger claiming she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. He repays it by handing her a ledger proving that a sanctioned oligarch's 'clean' fortune was built on a massacre her own agency helped bury, and that the assassin sent to retrieve the ledger has already killed twice. Hunted by the killer, disavowed by her agency, and blocked at every legal turn, Coral and Sable run a cross-border gauntlet through three jurisdictions to deliver the truth to an international tribunal. In the end Coral chooses truth over loyalty, testifies at the cost of her career, and Sable — revealed to be the massacre's lone survivor — finally stops running, while the assassin, exposed by the very ledger he hunted, is taken alive.
about_author: Dominic Delacroix is a former compliance auditor who traded boardrooms for backstreets, writing thrillers steeped in the gray mechanics of dirty money. He lives off-grid along the Atlantic coast, where he claims the best plots arrive with the fog.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Ten years of clean, boring casework crack open when Sable appears in her office claiming she saved his life in Lisbon — a debt she doesn't remember. He leaves a burner phone and a warning. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Sable returns with an encrypted ledger linking oligarch Vadim Krestov's fortune to a village massacre, and evidence her own agency signed off on the cover-up. That night her apartment is searched. Emotional beat: vertigo as her orderly world tilts.

chapters.title: Clean Money, Dirty Hands
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral traces the ledger's shell companies and confirms it's authentic — and that her mentor, Deputy Director Hale, appears in the chain. She tells no one. Emotional beat: the first crack of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Man Called Sable
chapters.summary: POV Sable. We learn Sable is Tomas Reyes, the massacre's sole survivor, who has spent fifteen years building his case. He chose Coral deliberately: she once flagged the account that briefly spared his family. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into patience.

chapters.title: Glass in the Doorway
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The assassin, Voss, makes his first attempt, killing Sable's courier. Coral realizes she's already inside the story whether she accepts it or not. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral maps the delivery options: a Hague tribunal intake, a Swiss banking inquiry, a US whistleblower channel — each compromised. Sable proposes the 'safehouse,' a dead-drop network he built years ago. Emotional beat: grim strategic clarity.

chapters.title: Hale's Handshake
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Hale summons Coral, offers a promotion and a warning dressed as kindness. She plays loyal while realizing the agency will bury her if she moves. Emotional beat: performing trust while swallowing revulsion.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable reveals the safehouse: a decommissioned lighthouse station in the Azores wired with redundant data caches. He explains the route and the rules. Coral sees the survivor beneath the operative. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership becoming trust.

chapters.title: Borderline
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The pair cross into Portugal under forged papers while Voss closes in, forcing them to abandon a planned handoff. Coral's tradecraft — reading money, reading people — saves them. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Costs
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable confesses the full massacre story, including the names of the dead — his family among them. Coral understands why he can't hand this to anyone who might bury it. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Swiss Detour
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A Zurich banker who can authenticate the ledger agrees to meet, then is found dead before the appointment — Voss is ahead of them. Coral realizes the ledger alone isn't enough; it needs a living witness. Emotional beat: the walls narrowing.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral is officially named a person of interest; her accounts are frozen and her photo circulates. Hale's message is unmistakable. She burns her old life deliberately. Emotional beat: liberation inside ruin.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: POV Voss. The assassin's chapter: a professional with a personal stake — his brother was on the cover-up's payroll and died of guilt. Voss wants the ledger not for money but to end it. Emotional beat: the hunter revealed as haunted.

chapters.title: Midwater
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A ferry crossing becomes a trap; Sable is wounded covering Coral's escape. She must choose the mission or the man. Emotional beat: love declared in the language of sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse
chapters.summary: POV Coral. They reach the Azores safehouse, upload the ledger to the dead-drop caches, and prepare the tribunal package. Voss arrives. Emotional beat: fragile hope under a tightening sky.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Station
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable confronts Voss — survivor and instrument of the same crime. Voss reveals Hale's people are already en route to seize the caches, and that he never intended to destroy the ledger. Emotional beat: enemies discovering a shared wound.

chapters.title: Three Governments Move
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Hale's extraction team, Portuguese police, and a US legal attaché converge on the island. Coral splits the caches, keeping the authenticating key on her body. Emotional beat: the gambit committed, no way back.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Captured by Hale's team, Coral is offered full reinstatement in exchange for silence. She hears Hale admit the cover-up on a live line Sable kept open. Emotional beat: loyalty dying so truth can breathe.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Sable and Voss, uneasy allies, extract Coral before she can be disappeared. Voss takes a bullet meant for Sable and survives, choosing to testify about his employers. Emotional beat: redemption bought in blood.

chapters.title: The Hague
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Before the tribunal intake, Coral delivers the ledger, the key, the live-line recording, and her sworn testimony. Hale is detained mid-flight; Krestov's assets freeze in real time. Emotional beat: quiet, ferocious vindication.

chapters.title: Interest Paid
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At the massacre memorial, Sable reads the victims' names aloud as the tribunal docket goes public. The debt he carried for fifteen years is finally settled. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into peace.

chapters.title: Sable and the Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Months later, stripped of her badge but not her purpose, Coral runs a private forensic practice; Sable tends the lighthouse station, now a real refuge for witnesses. A new stranger arrives with a favor that never happened. Emotional beat: the cycle continues — this time, on their terms.
